title: model-right-sizer Right-Sizing Blueprint (Pass A)
description: Strict output contract for the model-right-sizer agent's Pass A (the Right-Sizing Blueprint). The agent emits exactly one JSON object conforming to this schema instead of prose or markdown tables. See blueprint.example.json for a worked instance. additionalProperties is false at every level on purpose — an agent cannot reintroduce free-form fields.

schema_version.description: Bump alongside this file and the plugin CHANGELOG when the shape changes.

mode.description: dry_run = produced by the model-right-sizer-dryrun skill against a hypothetical intent; live_blueprint = produced as the front bookend of a real build.

intent.description: The free-text task or build this blueprint was produced for.

blueprint_rows.description: One row per decomposed stage/sub-agent this work will spend model tokens on. Carries the three-signal scoring.

work_routing_map.description: One row per execution/build unit — the 'who produces what' translation of the blueprint rows into dispatchable work. May be empty for a dry run with no build units yet decided.

message_schemas.description: One entry per distinct handoff-seam shape, referenced by id from blueprint_rows[].handoff_schema_ref and work_routing_map[].handoff_schema_ref. Do not author one per pair of stages — share an entry across seams with the same shape.

reason.description: One clause. Never a bare number.

model.description: A model ID from price_sheet.models[], or the literal 'deterministic_query_layer' when the pick is to route via a deterministic query layer instead of a model.

effort.description: Omit (or 'none') when model is 'deterministic_query_layer' or the model has no effort dial.

what_flips_it.description: The concrete condition that would flip primary and runner-up.

budget.description: token_ceiling is always required and always an actual integer, never null or omitted -- use 0 for a row that spends no model tokens at all (e.g. routed entirely through a deterministic query layer). This is what keeps 'budget: {}' or 'budget: {token_ceiling: null}' from satisfying the schema despite Pass A's 'not a vibe' requirement.

thinking_budget.description: e.g. '<=8k thinking'. Null only for a stage with no effort dial at all, or 0 token_ceiling.

query_shaped.description: True if this stage is fundamentally a structured-data query/computation (lookup, join, aggregate, arithmetic) rather than open-ended reasoning.

query_layer_note.description: Required-in-spirit when query_shaped is true: the deterministic-query-layer alternative and its expected token/reliability delta.

loop_class.description: single-shot / low-tool-turn (<=2 tool turns) vs agentic (>=3 tool turns / unattended multi-tool). Governs whether a down-pin is safe to ship live or must be measurement-gated.

signals.description: The three pillars. All three are required on every row — none may be omitted or left as a bare number.

default_model.description: The consuming system's static default for this role/stage, if one exists. Null if there is none.

handoff_schema_ref.description: An id into message_schemas[], or the literal 'none' (terminal stage, nothing downstream to hand off to), or 'route_via_query_layer'.

derived_from_stage_id.description: blueprint_rows[].id this build unit was decomposed from, if traceable to one.

status.description: Always 'not_started' as emitted by Pass A (nothing has been dispatched yet). The invoking session updates this in place as it dispatches and checks in on this unit, so the blueprint JSON doubles as a live status ledger it can report from on request instead of re-deriving status from scattered sub-agent threads. See 'Chief of staff' in model-right-sizer.md.

status_updated_at.description: An ISO-8601 UTC timestamp read from an actual clock (e.g. a shell `date -u` call) at the moment `status` was last set on this row -- never guessed or reasoned from memory of how many turns have passed. Null only while `status` is 'not_started' and no live dispatch/clock read has happened yet; any other status requires a real, freshly-read timestamp (enforced below). This is what lets a report distinguish a fresh 'in_progress' from a stale one -- without it, a row that finished between the last write and the next read reads as falsely still-running. On a status request, compare this against the current time: a status other than 'done'/'blocked' whose timestamp is old relative to how long that unit should take is 'unconfirmed, check again', not ground truth.

status_note.description: Free-text detail on the current status, e.g. why a row is 'blocked'. Null when status is self-explanatory.

seam_description.description: e.g. 'build stage -> review stage' or 'finder -> verifier fan-out'.

exclude.description: What this handoff must NOT carry, e.g. 'full transcript', 'raw retrieved rows', 'chain-of-thought', 'tool call logs'.

source.description: delegated_fetch = a sub-agent dispatch fetched live pricing; direct_fetch = this agent fetched it itself; fallback_snapshot = live retrieval failed, figures are the illustrative snapshot and unverified this run.

would_measure.description: The 2-3 things that would sharpen the next blueprint.

ledger_found.description: Whether a recommended-vs-actual calibration history was available and consulted.

adjusted_row_ids.description: blueprint_rows[].id / work_routing_map[].id values whose pick changed because of the calibration history.
